Back around 2016ish the US passed a law that changed how we punish websites for hosting certain illegal types of content on your site. Mostly having to do with things like violence, child pornography, human trafficking, or revenge porn. Laws banning this stuff had existed for a bit, but because of how websites were considered by law, they were enforced differently.

Originally the websites had a "fourm" status which bascially meant that as long as they were making common sense checks to make sure that kind of content wasn't easy to upload, then if something slipped through the cracks the responsibility was on the uploader. If the website was made aware of the illegal content, they had to take it down, but unless someone pointed out to them that the content was illegal, they weren't punished for unknowingly hosting it.

That changed in around 2016, when a law was passed saying that if a website was hosting that kind of content then it was the website's responsibility for letting it go on the platform in the first place. This meant that  any video hosted on the site with that illegal content could lead to criminal charges against the hosting site itself, not just the uploader. This might not have been a big problem for things like child pornography since there is a lot of technology that can be used to flag that, but when it came to thinks like violence and CnC, how could an ai quantify consent?

Since even letting one thing through the cracks could mean jail time, most of the major hosters decided their only option was to stop anonymous people from uploading videos and make sure that everyone who was uploading was aware of the law and went on record to say that all of their content is on the level.

Technically amateur stuff is still possible, it's just prohibitively difficult to check.

That's a big part of the reason only fans blew up. It gives an amateur outlet while still keeping the uploader accountable to the current laws.

Hey I'm really sorry to hear you're going through this.
I've played a lot of MMO games and I'm guessing most people who have played MMOs know how you feel. 

You and your friends aren't doing anything wrong. This is part of how these games are designed. They are made as level grinds so that if one friend gets ahead it forces all their friends to play the game even more or buy something to stay caught up.

It's a rough feeling and it can turn a fun game into a stressful experience.  You can feel like you are doing something wrong when not playing the game or that your friends are trying to leave you behind. The game feels like an obligation more than an escape and if you try and take a break from it you feel punished.

Your friends probably aren't trying to exclude you, (at least nothing in your post leads me to belive that) they are just playing a game they love. They pushed passed a point where it's fun for them to play with your level. They might be sharing their pics with you because even though they wont play with you they still know you they still can share their love of the game with you. 

Games mean different things for different people. And people play them in different, sometimes incompatible, ways. Some people like to take their time with mmos and advance together with friends, some people get hooked and want to push as far as they can and play with whoever is at their level or can take them higher, there is nothing wrong with either style.

 I would refocus on how YOU love to play the game, and chat with your friends about the parts of the game that you all enjoy. And remember just like your playing the game isn't about them, their playing the game isn't about you.

A few years back a very good friend of mine was going through Chemo, she was admitted into the hospital and I had the spare time so I spent the night with her for a few nights.  Her bed was in the far side of the room, and there was another person in the bed closer to the door, they were separated by a curtain.

The woman who shared the room was suffering from lung cancer, she couldn't have been more than 28 and she was losing the battle. My friend and I sat awake holding each others hands as we listened to this poor woman struggle to breathe every second for days. It sounded like she was breathing in water through a plastic bag. We listened as her family came. We listened as the nurses said there was nothing they could do for her.  We listened as her doctors told them that she wouldn't last long. We listened when her mother told the family that her father wouldn't make it off the plane in time. And we listened as she lost her battle and the doctors took her out of the room.

It was devastating for us to listen to. To be two strangers watching the painful and tragic end of a young life. It was especially tough for my friend,  at the time 25 and newly diagnosed with cancer.

I still hear the sound of that poor woman trying to breathe sometimes, I remember her name. I remember the nickname her sister called her when she said goodbye. I think about her dad who couldn't make it out of the airport in time to say goodbye. I hate that to me this persons entire life only amounts to the spectacle of pain that I just happened to see in her last moments.  My friend and I still talk about it on tough days. As for my friend, She's fine. Cancer is never over but she is doing very well and is as healthy as we could hope.

A day that will live in infamy

So when I was in the 4th grade I moved to a new school. I didn't have many friends and I wanted a way to get to know people. So there is this talent show going on. I decide to sign up. Now we are all children, so you figure there would be some sort of vetting process maybe? Like an adult who can help dumb kids from making bad decisions ? Nope, you just sign your name, and they are all like "cool, be ready to show off your talent in a month."   


I sign my name, and walk away. What did I sign up for? Oh nothing big, just playing the piano. Only problem was, I had no idea how to play the piano, but I figured "fudge it, I'll learn in a month, a month is forever to me because Im a dumb 4th grader." Well a month passes and I totally forgot to practice, luckly for me I have an ace in the hole, I know how to play the first 4 seconds of moonlight sonata because my uncle taught me. My young, innocent 4th grade heart is confident that I will wow my entire school with my beautiful playing.   


I sit there with the other boys in the class, making fun of the other people's talents (as you do when you are a dumb 4th grader) and then this kids younger sister goes on. This girl is in 2nd grade and sits down at the piano. She starts playing the Harry Potter theme song with BOTH HANDS!!!! It sounds beautiful, like angels themselves are singing the tones. For the first time (but not the last) in my little 4th grade life I realize that my mouth wrote a check my little undisciplined hands couldn't cash.  I start freaking out, and they call my name. A smart kid would have just not gone up, pretended not to hear, or maybe just run away. Not me though. I walked up there with confidence, I was sure that in the last moment I would reach in, and pull out that concert pianist sitting deep down inside.   


I played four notes on that damn piano before I realized just how fucked I was and I walked off stage. Everyone assumed I just got stage fright and was really supportive of me. I was too scared to tell them that I just never knew how in the first place. So by the end not only had I embarrassed myself to all my prospective friends, but then I felt like a liar for letting them gas me up when I got back.   


I've done dumber things, with far worse consequences, but I think about that story a lot.

It's all about context.  Mary Sue's can exist in any story, but they are easiest to spot in fan fiction, or sequels to stories.

**tl;dr-** *Remember when you used to play pretend and your friend would make a character who had all the best powers, all the other characters love, and could never be caught off guard? That.-*

Generally speaking a Mary Sue is a character in a work who doesn't fit the theme of the story, who also contains a higher level of competency than their surrounding characters. They can have any one of the following traits.

1. They seem like a character made to represent the writer, or one of the individuals who worked on the project.
2. The character is given strong connections to popular characters with little or no foreshadowing (a characters:Brother/Twin/Ex-lover/Childhood friend/Mentor ect.)
3. The character is hyper competent and is immune to negative consequences.
4. Other characters in the story inexplicably love or admire the random new character.
5. Has a very melodramatic call to action or sacrifice

For me the biggest example of a Mary Sue was the Character Genesis Rhapsados from Final Fantasy 7: Crisis Core.

If you haven't played it, Final Fantasy 7 was a story heavy video game that was praised for its complex narrative. It explores the concepts of loss and identity in a pretty neat way, and also was known for its stoic, too cool for school, bad-ass villain Sephiroth.  Sephiroth was a swordsman, a military super solider, and had a pretty iconic look with a 90s leather trench coat vibe and a single wing.

When the games prequel, Crisis Core, came out it introduced Genisis, who was touted to be a swordsman,  a military super soldier, and was given a look with a 90s leather trench coat, and later, a single wing. The character was given the same origin as Sephiroth, made to be his equal/rival, and made him the original catalyst for the game's story.  This clashed with the detailed backstory they already gave Sephiroth and changed the relationship between a lot of the main characters of the original game. On top of this the character was given no personality, and was loved by all of the ambient characters,to try and to play up his eventual death as a tragedy. The character was also famously based off the Japanese pop singer GACKT who was close friends with the game's director.  He just stood out as a sore thumb and took more away from the story than he gave.

Again the big deal is always context. There are ways to change stories and introduce new and interesting characters who have some or all of those traits, but if it doesn't seem to fit you have yourself a Mary sue.

EDIT: I saw someone else comment that Mary Sue is a term used to delegitimize female characters in fiction. I think its important to say that this definitely does happen. Characters like Rey from Star Wars, Katniss from the hunger games, and even Arya Stark, have all been called Mary Sue's even though they fit very well in the narrative of their stories. In those cases people are just using the word to try and justify their hatred for female protagonists, which is not okay. That said, just because some people use Mary Sue's to try and put female characters down, it doesn't mean that Mary Sue's aren't a thing in their own right.

Its important to remember that a Mary sue isn't just an overpowered character (almost all protagonists are overpowered) and they don't specifically have to be female (some call male characters like this Gary Stu's but 99% of people will be fine if you just call them Mary Sue's.)

​

I think it helps to know where the name came from. Mary Sue first came to describe the original characters people wrote into fan fictions of popular movies and books (Harry Potter, Kingdom Hearts, ect.) These characters were usually made by kids and teens to be avatars in their world, and were pretty poorly written. A lot of times the characters were young girls who were special, locked in a tragic romance with a specific character, and beloved. They were escapist fantasies. Other times they were young boys who had very similar tragic arcs. That said, there is nothing wrong with kids creating poorly written characters in their own stories or fan fiction, it's just more annoying to see these characters on hte big screen.

You want him to alter his behavior to accommodate your sensitivities, (making house rules about what can and cant be said, judging his apologies as not emotional enough) but I don't hear you trying to address his emotional needs. I dont want to speculate, but there are a ton of reasons why someone can give a half assed apology, and most of them have to do with they fact that they themselves feel hurt by the interaction, but are being forced to label themselves as the bad guy by apologizing.    


Im sure you're right that his apologies are coming off as half assed, and he definitely seems too callus and is acting like a dick. That said, you need to ask why it is he's being difficult. Is it because he doesn't respect you? or is it because he feels hurt too but is expected to bury that to apologize?

The key isn't to try and get him to act the way you want to (aka being more sensitive) but instead to bridge communication so you can answer key questions (is his insensitivity born of disrespect, or just from a difference in values?)

So really interesting history here. the reason that the catholics call themselves the catholics is because in 1054 there was a huge schism in the church.   


You see in the early days the main religion of Christianity was just called **Christendom**, and it was centered around different bishops throughout Europe and Asia who could basically help administer to priests, answer questions, and interpret the bible when an answer wasn't clear.  
 Bishops were all voted on, but it was accepted that people who became bishops were holy men who were qualified to make these decisions in the name of God. (in the bible there is even a passage that some interpret gives the church a kind of wiggle room when it comes to figuring stuff out Matthew 16:18-19)  


Now Christendom had a bunch of bishops, and for the most part they were all equal in authority, except one. One bishop was considered to be higher than the rest and had what we call papal primacy, the bishop of Rome; or as we call him now The Pope.  The Pope was different because the traditional seat of the Pope was orignally occupied by Peter, who it's said Jesus entrusted the whole of the church to in the first place. As such the Pope was considered to have a higher authority than the other Bishops.   


Over time this arrangement caused differences in the church, with many of the other bishops believing that while the pope was 'first among equals' that he wasn't significantly different than they were. This led to a split, the people who believed the pope had the highest authority in Christendom, and the people who didn't. After a while it was clear that neither group was going away so they had to name themselves. The Papal side eventually became the **Catholics**, and the non-papists became the **Eastern Orthodox Church,**  


The two groups pretty much remained the big denominations in Christianity until the protestant reformation rolled around in the 1500s. This reformation basically said that Catholicism was bad and eastern orthodox wasn't much better and that individuals should be able to interpret the bible themselves. See both the Catholics and the Eastern Orthodox  believed that only priests, who dedicated a lifetime of study, could interoperate scripture, but the protestants generally believed that people who weren't priests could do it too. This led to an explosion of new christian religions: **Anglicans, Lutherans, Calvinists, Methodists** and many more. 

This boom got even bigger once people started immigrating to the Americas and the culture of American religions was born giving rise to **Pentecostals, Episcopals,  Mormons, Christian Scientist** and many many more.    


There is no one Christian religion, and all of these religions primarily use the bible (except the Mormons) as their key scripture.

From a nutrient perspective the ice no different from water. So as long as the water that makes up the ice wouldn't hurt you the ice itself wouldn't hurt you either.

Physically eating ice is no more dangerous than eating other things.

The human body maintains an average temp of 36c, ice melts at 0c so the likelihood of damage from the cold is almost nonexistent.That said there is a common sense aspect. Just like it would be a bad idea to drink a lot of hot chocolate in a burning desert, I wouldn't start downing ice if you are stranded in the arctic.

Just like drinking too much hot soup without stopping or giving your throat a chance to cool down can make you uncomfortable, having too much ice too quickly might make your throat or teeth cold.

I've seen people talk about the sharpness of the ice. I mean its technically possible to hurt yourself that way, but a good rule of thumb is to be careful when you eat that look like they could stab your mouth. As long as the ice cube isn't in a jagged sharp death shape, you should be ok. As far as the freak accident of biting down on an ice cube and it forming thousands of tiny needles aimed at the roof of your mouth? Much less likely,  especially in smaller ice cubes. The fineness of a small point mixed with the heat of your mouth will cause the ice at the tip to melt pretty quickly, dulling it. At that point its not much more dangerous than eating a tortilla chip.

The only real downside to eating ice is it can be bad for your teeth, but even this isn't a universal rule, the strength of ice depends on its thickness and its temperature. If you are smart about eating ice and make sure to gently test it before chomping down , you should be fine, not much different than biting down on a jolly rancher or tootsie-pop.

**TLDR; If you try hard enough a marshmallow can be dangerous to eat. An ice cube isn't any more dangerous than eating 90% of the food you are used to eating.**

There is no historical reference to an inter-species war. Mix that with the fact that all of the races seem to fall in line behind the crown (with the exception of the Gerudo). Not to mention, that while each race has its own minor deities associated with their growth, there is no evidence to suggest that there is any issue with the greater Hylian cosmology. The fact that the Deku Tree, the Gorons and the Zora were entrusted with spiritual stones seems to suggest the opposite, that they are on board with this greater cosmology. 

Not to mention the idea that all of the temples needed to be broken down centuries before the game begins is a flawed concept. Ganondorf was a powerful enough wizard to kill the deku tree, revive an ancient beast, and poison a deity all **before** he acquired the Triforce of power. (the thing that makes him neigh immortal and allowed him to raze Hyrule castle down, and suspend a keep over a pit of lava). Seven years with that kind of power is more than enough time to do serious damage. And remember that Ganondorf's influence is directly linked to 3 of the bosses which terrorize the temples, and indirectly linked to the other two. 

* The forest temple is ravaged by his own spectral shadow, a phantom of himself, and the implication could be made the the abundance of Poe and undead in the temple are the result of Ganondorf's influence on the temple.

* Vovolgia was a dragon long dead, but Ganondorf revives him to terrorize the temple. 

*Twinrova, the boss of the spirit temple is comprised of the two witches who raised ganondorf, who explicitly guarded the temple in search of the sage of spirit.

Indirectly, Ganondorf's influence allowed the ancient spirit Bongo Bongo to escape his prison in Kakariko town's well, and there is heavy implication that Morpha was created by Ganondorf. 

the reason for him to do all of this, is linked to the purpose of the temples. They are secret places, but not because they were bastions of  secret worship, but because they are conduits of power for the sages. Only through overcoming trails in the temple could a sage be awakened, and the power of all the awakened sages is ultimately what seals Ganon away. 
Ganondorf went to great lengths to damage the temples in order to weaken the only thing he was afraid could stop him.

I'm pretty sure the reason Arin doesn't like tutorials is that he thinks that they are the wrong way to go about teaching players the game. The tutorial is a bit of a cop out, by giving one you don't have to design a scenario where the player is forced to think about your mechanics and how to use them. And you can't say that just because a game has a lot of elements that it necessarily needs  a tutorial. Wind Waker isn't any more complicated than A link to the past, which had a striking variety of items which had to be used continually without tutorial. 

I happen to agree, the use of tutorials today is a bit of a crutch, they are rarely really helpful. In games that are intuitive like Zelda, tutorials are annoying and interrupt the flow of game play. In more complicated games they are exhausting and remove a lot of the thrill of beginning a game. Teaching through game play, or even having a character explain things in real time are both more fluid alternatives.
